correctness.rationale: On A^2_alpha, alpha>-1, s>=2 and fixed nonnegative m,n, normalized monomial vs orthonormal slants have asymptotic product coefficients c=s^(alpha+1) and c=1, respectively. Their two product supports are residue classes rhoA=-n-sm and rhoB=-m-sn mod s^2. Gamma-moment ratios give norm-compact tail errors to c(S^a V_rhoA^* - S^b V_rhoB^*). The supports agree exactly iff s^2 divides m-n because gcd(s-1,s^2)=1. For distinct classes CC* is 2c^2 I in the Calkin algebra; otherwise it is c^2(2I-U^d-U^-d), d nonzero, giving respectively singleton {2c^2} or interval [0,4c^2]. Infinite kernels enforce zero in sigma_e(|C|) in the first case; m=n zero. Thus both essential norms sqrt(2)c or 2c and |C| spectra are reconstructed; ordinary nonnormal C spectrum is NOT claimed. Original check_slant.py was read and its coefficient/support logic inspected; its finite 184k assertions do not prove the all-index limit.

value.rationale: This is a motivated exact operator-theoretic classification of noncompact analytic monomial slant commutators, detecting a nontrivial s^2 divisibility boundary and a change in the topology of the Calkin positive spectrum. The two canonical slant normalizations are carefully distinguished. Quantified essential norm/spectral types have independent utility beyond a yes/no commutativity criterion.

limitations: Only analytic monomial symbols, fixed s and alpha>-1; not general symbols, ordinary commutator spectrum, or parameter-uniform estimates.
